facts.raw_span: A 28-year-old G2P1 woman presented 31 days after an elective cesarean delivery
with worsening headache and easy fatigability for 3 days
The headache was continuous, global, and had become severe over 24 hours
associated with nausea and malaise
Vital signs were normal
She was fully conscious and oriented
all meningeal signs were negative
motor function was intact
Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count
prothrombin time, partial prothrombin time, and international normalized ratio
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection
measuring 15 mm in width with a 13-mm midline shift

facts.raw_span: A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Antrum: normal appearance
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
foveolar hyperplasia
Layer contours slightly disorganized with mild lymphocytic infiltration
H+/K+-ATPase staining: heterogeneously reduced
Anti-parietal cell antibody: <1:10 (negative)
Serum gastrin: 150 pg/mL (normal 37–172)
Anti-H. pylori IgG: <3 U/mL (negative)

facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man presented with a painful nodule on the lower part of his right leg
the lesion had been stable in size and painless for 4 years but had enlarged and become tender over the past 6 months
No history of trauma or personal or family history of malignancy
an irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm was noted just above the lateral malleolus of the right leg
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy was present
there were no other suspicious cutaneous lesions
Routine blood tests, including complete blood count, fasting blood sugar, liver and renal function tests, were within normal limits
Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV were negative
a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass partly covered by skin, measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields
Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45
